evidence:
Row 52 task_security_and_secrets: workbook Quality Checks row 52 reads 'No live credentials, real personal data, host paths, unpinned remote fetch, or injection payload anywhere in the task.' The Internal Quality Checks annotation for 52 says credentials or real-person data may be added for third-party integrations and are removed before client delivery. Skill quality-checks.md section 52 treats a live credential in task.toml or the brief as a delivery-time Note, but still flags real secrets or personal data in seed data, the solution or an image. SKILL.md known false positives cover demo passwords and ${VAR} templates.
Frozen task (.qc-cache/hireops-lessons-2026-10-08-r6/task), every file scanned:
(1) Credentials. No provider key, PEM, JWT, AWS, GitHub or Slack token shapes anywhere. task.toml:30-35 [verifier.env] uses ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN = "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}" and an empty ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, which is the frozen template block. The only password is the documented demo credential Hireops!2026: instruction.md:19, environment/instructions/hireops_rules.md:11, tests/app_context.md:8 and solution/app/src/db.js:63 ('Public demo credential given in the brief'). The seed data has no password field; db.js:66 assigns the demo password at insert. Session tokens come from crypto.randomBytes at runtime (src/index.js:88), not literals. tests/Dockerfile writes only a codex config (model_reasoning_effort, approval_policy, sandbox_mode), with no secret, and is byte-identical to the template.
(2) Personal data. environment/assets/seed_data.json is byte-identical to solution/app/src/seed_data.json (cmp). It has 10 users, 3 jobs, 16 applications, 127 messages and 3 notes. Every one of its 22 email addresses uses an RFC 2606 reserved domain (hireops.example, candidates.example, mail.example). It has no phone numbers, addresses or ID numbers. Messages are templated synthetic lines such as 'Could you share your availability for next week? (#003)', and notes are short synthetic recruiter remarks. Names are generic personas, with nothing that identifies a real individual.
(3) Host paths. A grep for drive letters, /Users/, /home/, Documents, turing-workspace, AppData or UNC paths found nothing. Container paths are only /app, /assets, /instructions, /tests, /logs/verifier, /tmp/submission and /proc in solve.sh, which scans process file descriptors so the DB reset is safe.
(4) Remote fetch. The only URLs in the task are https://openrouter.ai/api (frozen task.toml:33 judge endpoint) and http://localhost:3000 or 127.0.0.1:3000 (all five prompt.md files, app_context.md:4, test.sh:48/136). Judge prompts contain no public internet address (Colderwater lesson 13 checked). The solution has no external URL or CDN load, index.html loads only /js/*.js, and the bootstrap.js:28 proxy targets 127.0.0.1 only. npm installs are version-pinned: express@5.1.0, better-sqlite3@12.4.1, @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.281, @openai/codex@0.151.0 and @playwright/mcp@0.0.79. pip uses harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7, and Chromium is installed via the pinned playwright CLI. Base images use tags (node:22-bookworm-slim, python:3.12-slim) rather than digests, but environment/Dockerfile, tests/Dockerfile, test.sh, score.py, restart_mcp.py and .dockerignore are byte-identical to rules/projects/webdev-task-template (diff), so they are template-controlled and not editable here. Under the public-network profile this is not a task defect.
(5) Injection. A scan of seed free text found no HTML/script, template syntax, SQL or 'ignore previous / system prompt / judge / grader' strings. Grep across instruction, rules, app_context, prompts and judge.toml found no instruction aimed at the judge or builder that would subvert grading. The only 'judge' text is the legitimate grading instructions.
Adversarial checks. A broken app cannot exploit anything in these task files to pass. A conforming app is not penalised by any security-related demand. A real-secret leak would require a literal key in task.toml, and none exists. Delivery-time strip: nothing to strip beyond the template ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY} placeholder.
